sector_model: equipment rental: P/E, price to book, EV/Adjusted EBITDA, gross rental capex, net debt, utilization; FCF burdened by growth capex
thesis: McGrath RentCorp (Nasdaq: MGRC) rents modular buildings, portable storage and test equipment (TRS-RenTelco) and builds modular units (Enviroplex). Q3 2026: revenue 274.6M (+7%), net income 48.8M ($2.00 vs $1.72, +15%), Adjusted EBITDA 106.5M (+10%). Segments: TRS-RenTelco rental revenue +26%, Adj EBITDA +27% (data center projects), Mobile Modular rental +4% but EBITDA -3% and sales -10%, Portable Storage rental -3% and EBITDA -20% in soft demand. Nine months: revenue 694.3M (+1.0%), NI 109.5M (+2.8%), EPS 4.46 vs 4.32. Guidance 2026: revenue cut to 945-960M, Adj EBITDA 365-373M, gross rental equipment capex raised sharply to 270-290M. Nine month OCF 178.0M versus rental equipment purchases 218.7M and other capex 38.0M: FCF about -78.7M (approximate, sales proceeds not netted); notes payable rose to 618.3M from 514.9M, plus a 75M 6.53% Series H note on 2026-11-02 (8-K). Equity 1.278B, debt/equity 0.48. Close 129.98 on 2026-11-12: market cap 3.17B, 20.0x TTM EPS 6.49, 2.5x book, about 10.3x EV to guided Adj EBITDA, dividend 1.98 (1.5%). Reasonable valuation for a cyclical lessor but the case rests on TRS data center rentals while debt funds capex; no clear mispricing.
counterthesis: Earnings quality is rental growth in one segment (TRS) that depends on data center and electronics demand, while the two largest legacy businesses are flat to weak; revenue guidance was cut. Capex is being raised by about 70M while FCF is negative and debt rose 103M in nine months, with only 1M cash; the new notes cost 6.53%, above the equity yield. Net income growth of 2.8% in nine months does not justify 20x. Management transition (CEO) adds uncertainty. Used equipment sale gains, depreciation assumptions and fleet quality were not examined, so earnings may be overstated if equipment lives are long. Peers, MD&A, debt note covenant ratios and 10-K were not read.
invalidation: Valuation case would require a price near 14-15x earnings or evidence that TRS capex earns returns well above 6.5% cost of debt. Thesis fails if TRS utilization and yield roll over, Mobile Modular rental turns negative, net debt/Adj EBITDA rises above about 2x, or covenant headroom narrows.
